Table from a List of Arrays

Source: R/figure-data.R
PlotDataFromArrays.Rd

Turns a named list of equally long arrays, for example the arrays of a NumPy .npz archive, into a data frame. Given a file path instead of a list, only the arrays needed are read with cellspecR::cs_read_npz() (pure R). One-dimensional arrays become columns, the columns of matrices become further columns, arrays defined only for some rows (masked) are expanded with NA, and rows can be restricted to a logical array.

Usage

PlotDataFromArrays(
  arrays,
  columns = NULL,
  matrices = NULL,
  masked = NULL,
  keep = NULL,
  row_id = NULL,
  row_base = 0L,
  row_first = FALSE
)

Arguments

arrays

Named list of vectors and matrices with one row per record, or the path of an .npz archive.

columns

Names of one-dimensional arrays to keep; a named vector or list renames them (new name = array name). Default all vectors of the record length.

matrices

Named list: for each matrix, either the new column names or list(names_from = "<array>", prefix = "") taking the names from a character array.

masked

Named list: output column (as named in columns) to the name of the logical array marking the rows its values belong to.

keep

Optional name of a logical array; only rows where it is TRUE are returned.

row_id

Optional name of a column holding the position of each row in the arrays (before keep).

row_base

Position of the first row (0 or 1).

row_first

Put the row_id column first instead of last.

Value

A data frame.

See also

Other plot-data builders: PlotDataBindRows(), PlotDataConstant(), PlotDataCount(), PlotDataCrossShares(), PlotDataDirection(), PlotDataDominant(), PlotDataJoin(), PlotDataKeyColours(), PlotDataLabels(), PlotDataLonger(), PlotDataMembership(), PlotDataPairRatio(), PlotDataProduct(), PlotDataQuantiles(), PlotDataRankRows(), PlotDataRatio(), PlotDataRecode(), PlotDataRelative(), PlotDataSelect(), PlotDataShares(), PlotDataSummarise(), PlotDataUnite()

Examples

a <- list(xy = matrix(1:6, 3), label = c("a", "b", "a"), names = c("u", "v"),
          feat = matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1, 2, 3), 3), kept = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE),
          cls = c(7L, 8L), has_cls = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE))
PlotDataFromArrays(a, columns = "label",
                   matrices = list(xy = c("x", "y"), feat = list(names_from = "names")))
#>   label x y   u v
#> 1     a 1 4 0.1 1
#> 2     b 2 5 0.2 2
#> 3     a 3 6 0.3 3
PlotDataFromArrays(a, c(type = "label", cls = "cls"), masked = list(cls = "has_cls"),
                   keep = "kept", row_id = "row")
#>   type cls row
#> 1    a   7   0
#> 2    a   8   2
